name: Havering

licensing.selective: Selective licensing started on 18 March 2026 in seven of the borough's 20 wards: Beam Park, Harold Wood, Rainham and Wennington, Rush Green and Crowlands, Squirrels Heath, St Albans, and St Edwards. Licences run for up to five years.
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing also started on 18 March 2026, for shared houses and flats with three or four people from two or more households.

housing: Havering has the highest rate of home ownership in London, and only about one household in six rented privately in 2021, though that share grew over the decade. Most homes are inter-war semis and terraces with gardens, alongside the large post-war Harold Hill estate and flats around Romford town centre. New-build estates at Beam Park and other sites in the south of the borough are adding homes. Since March 2026 the council licenses HMOs borough-wide and runs selective licensing in seven wards.
checkinTips: Inter-war semis and terraces with gardens: photograph the lawn, fences, gates, sheds and any garage, as gardens are a common check-out dispute.
Driveways and dropped kerbs: photograph the drive surface, any oil stains and the front wall at check-in.
Former council houses in Harold Hill: photograph the boiler, radiators and windows, and any damp in bathrooms and bedrooms.
Flats above shops in Romford: photograph the rear entrance, external stairs and bin area, and count the keys for every door.
New-build homes at Beam Park and Rainham: photograph flooring joints, worktops and any snagging marks, and record parking-permit and fob details.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions to Havering Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and use Housing Act 2004 notices against landlords.
